headline: MONTE ALTO RARE EARTH INDICATED RESOURCE SURGES 41% — BRE HITS 3.5MT AT 10.7% TREO, 3.1M KG DYSPROSIUM OXIDE
snippet: Brazilian Rare Earths (ASX: BRE) released a major mineral resource upgrade at Monte Alto, Bahia, Brazil on October 26: indicated ultra-high-grade tonnes grew 41% to 3.5 Mt at 10.7% TREO, and the Monte Alto South block roughly tripled its indicated tonnage to 1.9 Mt after intersecting thick, stacked mineralised horizons. The total (indicated plus inferred) resource grew 29% to 4.4 Mt at 9.9% TREO. Critical magnet metals within the estimate include approximately 3.1 million kg of dysprosium oxide and 572,000 kg of terbium oxide — the specific heavy rare earths at the center of Western defence and clean-energy supply chain policy. The estimate is based on more than 43,000 metres of diamond drilling, the deposit remains open to the south, north and east, and the Concentrate Sales Feasibility Study is targeted for delivery by end-2026.

headline: ABRASILVER DRILLS PROJECT-BEST 228M AT 1.79 G/T OXIDE GOLD — 66M AT 4.04 G/T AT OCULTO EAST, DIABLILLOS
snippet: AbraSilver Resource Corp. (TSX: ABRA) reported the best gold intercept drilled to date at Oculto: hole DDH-26-061 returned 228 metres at 1.79 g/t gold in oxide mineralization, including a high-grade core of 66 metres at 4.04 g/t gold — extending the Oculto East target beyond the current pit-constrained resource footprint at its Diablillos silver-gold project in Argentina's Puna region. The oxide character of the 228-metre intercept is the critical investment-case element: near-surface oxide gold at Diablillos carries materially lower processing costs than sulphide mineralisation and directly supports the open-pit heap-leach economics underpinning the project's bankability. The result is the standout of the 2026 drill program and sets up a potential resource expansion in the next estimate update.

headline: AGNICO +3.3%, GOLD FIELDS +3.2% MONDAY PREMARKET — GOLD RECOVERS TO $4,020 AS MINING EQUITIES BOUNCE BEFORE FOMC
snippet: Gold and silver miners bounced Monday premarket as spot gold climbed back to $4,020 from its lowest level since mid-July set the previous session, with the recovery driven by a softer U.S. dollar and easing oil prices reducing near-term inflation expectations. Agnico Eagle Mines (TSX/NYSE: AEM) gained 3.3%, Gold Fields 3.2%, AngloGold Ashanti and Sibanye-Stillwater each up approximately 2.8%. In London, Fresnillo rose 2.35% and Endeavour Mining 1.27%. The bounce follows a week of sustained selling pressure as investors positioned defensively ahead of the October 28 FOMC decision under new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh, whose September unanimous rate hike signalled the Trump administration's inflation fight is unfinished. GDX and GDXJ remain near 12-week lows in absolute terms despite the premarket recovery, reinforcing the historically wide gap between gold's price near $4,000 and gold miners' compressed valuations.

headline: GOLD STRIKE FLORIN YIELDS 400M AT 0.53 G/T FROM SURFACE IN FIRST 2026 HOLE — 50M AT 1.07 G/T, YUKON
snippet: Gold Strike Resources (TSXV: GSR) reported first assay results from its 2026 drill program at the Florin Gold Project in the Yukon: the lead hole returned 400 metres of 0.53 g/t gold from near surface, including a 50-metre interval grading 1.07 g/t gold. Florin hosts a pit-constrained Inferred resource of 2.507 million ounces, open in all directions and at depth. The 400-metre continuous near-surface intercept is the key data point for bulk-tonnage open-pit economics — consistent grade over very wide intervals from surface is the geometry heap-leach feasibility models reward. Gold Strike completed 11 holes totalling 4,014 metres in the 2026 campaign before breakup, and assays for the remaining holes are pending.

headline: LIBERTY GOLD OPENS 50,000-METRE BLACK PINE PROGRAM — FIRST 2026 ASSAYS IN FOR 5M-OZ IDAHO OXIDE GOLD PROJECT
snippet: Liberty Gold Corp. (TSX: LGD) released initial assay results from its 2026 drill program at the Black Pine Oxide Gold Project in southeastern Idaho — the first batch of results from a 50,000-metre campaign that is the largest in Black Pine's history. The program targets infill drilling to convert resources from indicated to measured category, resource-growth step-outs near planned mining areas, and engineering and permitting support work feeding a feasibility study. Black Pine hosts an Indicated Resource of 502.7 million tonnes at 0.30 g/t gold (4.88 million oz) plus Inferred Resource of 157.1 Mt at 0.21 g/t gold — one of the largest advanced-stage oxide gold deposits in the western United States.

headline: AUREKA SHAREHOLDERS GREENLIGHT A$8.9M FIDDLERS CREEK ACQUISITION — VICTORIAN GOLD MINE AND WEDDERBURN MILL CLOSE OCTOBER 30
snippet: Aureka Ltd. (ASX: AKA) shareholders voted on October 23 to approve the A$8.9 million acquisition of High Grade Holdings, owner of the producing Fiddlers Creek underground gold-silver mine and the Wedderburn gold processing mill in Victoria, Australia — with deal completion and settlement expected on or around October 30. The acquisition is structured as A$2.5 million cash and approximately A$6.4 million in Aureka shares, funded by a A$5.65 million placement. Fiddlers Creek has been in production since July 2025, and the Wedderburn mill (42,000 t/yr stated capacity) already processes its ore under an existing offtake arrangement. For Aureka, the transaction creates a vertically integrated gold producer in Victoria: the Fiddlers Creek mine feeds the Wedderburn mill, and Aureka's own Comstock and Irvine exploration projects can be toll-milled through it under an agreement signed in July 2026.

headline: HUDBAY AND MITSUBISHI PULL TRIGGER ON COPPER WORLD FID — 102K T/YR ARIZONA MINE AT $1.65/LB CASH COST TARGETS 2029
snippet: Hudbay Minerals (TSX/NYSE: HBM) and its 30% joint venture partner Mitsubishi Corporation formally approved construction of the Copper World project in Arizona on October 21 — the final investment decision for one of the most significant new copper developments in the United States. The definitive feasibility study projects average production of approximately 102,000 tonnes of copper per year over the first ten years (an 11% increase from the 2023 pre-feasibility study) at average cash costs of $1.65 per pound, positioning Copper World as one of the lowest-cost open-pit copper operations in the U.S. The project's base case uses a 15-year mine plan requiring only state and local permits — a structurally important distinction as federal permitting risk has delayed or killed several western U.S. copper projects. First production is targeted for the second half of 2029. The FID arrives as LME copper has retreated approximately 4% from its September 2026 all-time high of $14,875/tonne, in a week when Teck's Highland Valley Copper is also offline on strike — a dual supply disruption that reinforces the long-term copper deficit thesis underpinning the Copper World investment case.

headline: SP ANGEL MONDAY MARKET VIEW: GOLD OVERSOLD INTO FOMC, WARSH RATE PATH, MINERS DIVERGING FROM SPOT
snippet: London-based mining broker SP Angel published its Monday October 26 morning market note covering precious metals, base metals and junior mining equities ahead of the October 28 FOMC decision. The note addresses the divergence between gold's near-$4,000 spot price and continued compression in gold mining equity valuations — a spread that SP Angel's institutional clients track for tactical entry signals. With new U.S. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's September rate hike still fresh and markets pricing roughly 90% probability of a hold at October 28, the note contextualises the week's binary outcome for gold and silver miners and reviews key company news across London-listed mining names. SP Angel is one of London's leading mining-specialist broker-dealers and its morning notes are read by institutional and high-net-worth investors across the UK and European junior mining markets.

headline: ASX MINERS CLAW BACK MONDAY LOSSES — GOLD AND BASE METAL STOCKS RECOVER AS PRECIOUS METALS REBOUND
snippet: Australian mining stocks staged a recovery on Monday October 26 after early session selling pressure, with Stockhead's closing bell wrap noting gold and base metal names doing the heavy lifting to pull the ASX resources index back from its session lows. The intraday reversal tracked global precious metals prices recovering above $4,015 gold and $54 silver from the prior session's multi-month lows, as Asian equity markets stabilised and pre-FOMC positioning unwound some short positions. For ASX-listed junior gold explorers and uranium developers, Monday's price action — bouncing off oversold technical levels ahead of a known binary catalyst in the October 28 FOMC decision — continues the pattern seen across TSX-V and London-listed mining equities, where institutional buyers are re-entering near multi-month lows rather than waiting for the Fed decision outcome.
